string-array.name: help_fuel_level
string-array.item: Fuel level in the tank, in percent.
On slopes, in turns and when accelerating the value wanders — the fuel sloshes in the tank.
Doesn\'t change although fuel is being used, or jumps for no reason — the tank level sensor.

string-array.name: help_l100
string-array.item: Instant fuel consumption in liters per 100 km. The app calculates it from the hourly rate and speed, and shows it from 10 km/h.
The app has no reference consumption for this car. Accelerating briefly gives very large numbers — this is normal.
If the ECU doesn\'t report fuel rate, the app estimates it from MAF — this is approximate. Check against fill-ups: full tank, distance, liters.

string-array.name: help_lph
string-array.item: Fuel consumption in liters per hour: how much fuel goes into the engine right now, regardless of speed.
No reference for this car. Higher at cold idle than at warm idle — that\'s the warm-up.
If the name says \"from MAF\", consumption is calculated from air flow; with a dirty MAF it will be off too.

string-array.name: help_trim
string-array.item: Total fuel trim for the bank — short term plus long term. Shows how much the ECU has to correct the base fuel delivery based on the front O2 sensors. Bank 1 is cylinders 1-3-5, bank 2 is cylinders 2-4-6.
The common rule of thumb for any engine: within ±5% is good, up to ±10% is acceptable. Both banks should be close to each other. We don\'t know the thresholds at which this car\'s ECU sets a code.

Positive — lean mixture, the ECU adds fuel: air leak, dirty MAF, weak fuel delivery. Negative — rich mixture: leaking injector, EVAP purge. Codes: P0171/P0174 — lean, P0172/P0175 — rich. Banks differ — a problem on one bank (intake, injector, that bank\'s O2 sensor). Both moved together — a common cause (MAF, fuel pressure).
